facts.text: Monte Carlo simulations were used to induce and vary chemical short-range order in the HfNbTaTiZr alloy model.
The simulated structures were constrained to remain within a single-phase bcc model.
Lattice heat transport was evaluated using non-equilibrium molecular dynamics over a room-to-high-temperature regime.
Chemical short-range ordering produced HfTi and TiZr clusters with B2-like local structures.
The ordered binary clusters formed percolating pathways that facilitated lattice heat transport.
Short-range order reduced lattice distortion and therefore reduced phonon scattering relative to the random-alloy state.
The benefits of reduced lattice distortion and conductive percolation pathways outweighed the additional scattering caused by the ordered clusters themselves.
Short-range ordering modified the high-frequency phonon density of states.
Chemical short-range order increased lattice heat conductivity relative to the random-alloy baseline.
The lattice heat conductivity increased by approximately 12% relative to the random-alloy state.
Atomic displacements were reduced by approximately 12.5% compared with the random-alloy state.
